label: churn100-s3
summary: The churn model (training AUC 0.899) is a sum of log-odds terms. Its strongest term is a ramp on total day minutes: for the typical customer it switches on between 205 and 210 minutes, and risk rises from 3% at 200 minutes to 81% at 300; switching it off lowers AUC to 0.793. Customer service calls add risk through a direct edge and a hinge that acts on 100% of the 848 customers with 3 or more calls (risk 4% at 2 calls, 23% at 4); calls also weaken the day-minutes ramp, so the two effects add less than their sum. An international plan raises the typical risk from 3% to 24% (more in Connecticut, fitted to 7 rows), and a voice-mail plan lowers it from 3% to 1%. State enters as a per-state offset: several state gates are large constants that their own direct state edges largely cancel; the remaining offsets, from -4.51 (Vermont) to -1.53 (California), rest on a few dozen customers per state.

The summary template contains probe input values (205, 210, 200, 300 day minutes; 3, 2, 4 service calls) that --render reports as bare typed numbers because it has no allow list; they are chosen sweep inputs, not computed values, and are allow-listed the same way in the stored hypotheses. The 90 unchecked free-text sentences are qualitative statements and the leaf names.
tool_bugs: query_probe stores only the first rows of a long sweep (a 51-state sweep stored rows up to about index 4 for part contributions), so placeholders to later rows were refused; worked around with a shorter state sweep. query_enumerate refuses the whole input space when any continuous input exists (no way to hold continuous inputs fixed), so state cells were checked with query_subgroup and a probe sweep instead. Placeholders cannot reference probe input values (rows[k].inputs...), so sweep inputs must be allow-listed literals. One batched --calls run of 70 add_evidence writes exceeded the 120 s shell timeout (it completed in the background).

refuted_and_fixed: international_plan_gate: first hypothesis said it adds risk for plan holders; the probe and subgroup showed it also acts on the 73 Connecticut non-holders, so the hypothesis was revised

state gates: first hypotheses read the gates as per-state risk raises; probes showed each gate is largely cancelled by the state's own direct edge, so they were rewritten as constants plus cancelling corrections
